title: Airline defends flyover for South Africa-New Zealand rugby game after low-flying planes cause alarm
content:
An airline has defended the safety of a ceremonial flyover at a rugby Test match after viral footage caused concern about how low the aircrafts passed over DHL Stadium in Cape Town, South Africa.

Flightradar24, a platform which tracks live flight data, calculated that two Airlink planes flew less than 50ft (15metres) over the 55,000-capacity stadium before Saturday’s second Test match between South Africa and New Zealand. Footage of the flyover went viral on social media, appearing to show the lead aircraft coming closest to the stadium.

Airlink, which also operated a flyover for the first Test between the two sides on August 22, said in a statement on Sunday that, according to its flight data, the manoeuvre was performed within the South African Civil Aviation Authority’s (SACAA) “approved and rehearsed safety altitude and speed limits.”

“Airlink notes the concerns expressed in various social media and online forums regarding yesterday’s formation flyby over Cape Town’s DHL Stadium,” reads a widely-reported statement, via Arrive Alive — a South African transport website.

The statement also said that the “flight demanded careful planning and rehearsal” due to the low altitude and 150-knot (278km/h) speed, and that the SACAA and Air Traffic Navigation Services “provided valuable guidance, approval and support” to ensure the flypast took place safely.

It added: “The two aircraft were flown by highly-experienced crew, with each comprised of three senior captains operating in the roles of commander, co-pilot and safety/technical officer.”

The Athletic contacted DHL Stadium officials for comment.

Flyovers have regularly taken place at South Africa matches, after a South African Airways 747 jet famously carried the message “Good luck Bokke” ahead of their 1995 World Cup final victory against New Zealand.

Airlink announced in June it would be the official carrier of the ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry 2026’ four-match Test series between South Africa and New Zealand. The airline is flying the squads, coaches, management and support staff of both teams.

New Zealand won the first match of this summer’s series 33-16, with South Africa levelling after Saturday’s 33-26 victory.
